opportunities.title: Henry Moore Grants

amount.raw: New Projects and Commissions: max £20,000; Acquisitions and Collections: max £20,000; Conferences, Lectures and Publications: max £5,000; Long-Term Research: max £20,000; Research and Travel: max £2,500

opportunities.eligibility_summary: UK and international non-profit organisations (established and operating in a non-profit capacity for at least 12 months) for New Projects and Commissions, Acquisitions and Collections, Conferences/Lectures/Publications, and Long-Term Research; individual sculpture historians, academics and conservators for the Research and Travel category only. Not available to individuals wishing to develop their own artistic practice.
opportunities.summary: Grants supporting the growth and development of sculpture across historical, modern and contemporary registers, and funding research that expands the appreciation of sculpture. Categories cover exhibitions, exhibition catalogues, commissions, conferences, research, non-commercial publications, and development of collections through acquisitions, conservation, cataloguing and display. Applications considered four times per year (Autumn, Winter, Spring, Summer rounds).

opportunities.title: Visiting Research Fellowships

amount.raw: Expenses allocation for travel and subsistence: UK up to £600, Europe up to £700, Rest of world up to £1,000; accommodation provided in Leeds or Hertfordshire for the duration of the fellowship

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Academics, curators working on historic and contemporary sculpture (Visiting Research Fellowships); artists developing their practice through research (Artist Research Fellowships); established scholars for longer six-week Senior Fellowships. Fellowship at Studios & Gardens only for projects related to Henry Moore.
opportunities.summary: Fellowships enabling artists and researchers to spend a month using the Henry Moore Institute facilities in Leeds or Studios & Gardens in Hertfordshire, including accommodation, travel and subsistence expenses. Currently closed for 2026/27; next round opens in spring 2027.

opportunities.title: Dissertation Prize

amount.raw: BA dissertation: £250 cash prize; MA dissertation: £250 cash prize; plus Henry Moore Institute publications to cover price value of £50, copies added to the Research Library, and publication of abstracts

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Open to BA and MA students of all disciplines whose dissertation was submitted within the past academic year at a UK university. Dissertations must relate directly to sculpture and not previously have been published.
opportunities.summary: Two annual prizes for outstanding writing on contemporary, modern or historical sculpture. The 2026 prize submissions will open in autumn 2026.
